name: Z-Ro
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 crunk — Z-Ro (the `houston-screw` lane's research section)
notes: ⛔ **`confidence` is `low`, following the research's medium-low rating** — "SUC affiliation and era documented; parameters inferred from the audible idiom" — with the 62–76 band flagged [LOW-CONF] as well. Sourced: the sung blues-gospel register, i–iv–V and i–VI–VII with gospel organ voicings, a sparse kit with 8th hats and very little fill activity, low velocity variance, a long sustained 808 *plus* played-bass-style motion on some records, 4-bar loops with real motion, sung hooks with wide range, and sung intro / 16–24 bar verses / sung 8-bar hooks / outro vamp. INFERRED: every probability, velocity tier and register bound. ⛔ **This is the only entry in this batch whose bass is `independent_riff`, and it is the sourced difference.** "Long sustained 808 plus played-bass-style motion on some records" is two low voices doing different things: the 808 stays legato at 16–32 carrying the tonic, while the played bass at 24–43 leaves the kick, drops `followRootsProb` to 0.72, takes P5/m7/M2 passing tones and anticipates at 0.2. Everywhere else in this lane the bass mirrors the kick because the record is a pedal; here it does not, because the research says a player is on it. ▶ **`blues` in `session.scales` is the word the research uses.** "Minor, blues-inflected" cannot be said with a key label — a key name in this dataset is a label, not a pitch — so it is said as a scale draw, alongside dorian and minor pentatonic. The i–iv–V family and seventh-heavy `extensions` are the same fact in the harmony. ▶ **Gospel organ voicings are `close`, against a lane that is `open`.** The genre's whole harmonic signature is strings spread wide down to 40; an organ is a stack of close voices in the mid, so this entry pulls back to `close` at 45–76 and pushes seventh colour to 0.42. It is the one place this model contradicts its parent, and the research is explicit about why. ▶ **"Very little fill activity" is authored where the fingerprint leaves room.** The fill cadence itself is fixed at 4/8 bars, so sparseness is carried by the roll: `gapProb` 0.60 — the second-gappiest here — and `rolls.freqPerBar` 0.15, the floor of this band. `velocityVar` 0.08 is the research's "low velocity variance". ▶ **The sung layer is the arrangement's top**, so the counter goes *above* the melody at +12 with `answer_lick` weighted highest and `densityRatio` up to 0.7 — the most active counter in this batch — and the outro is a vamp at 8–12 bars rather than the genre's 4–8. ⚠ **`melody.timbreHint` is inherited rather than authored.** The genre's `church_organ` was chosen partly *from* this entry's gospel organ; overriding it here would restate the parent. ⚠ **The i–iv family is INFERRED** — the research names i–iv–V and i–VI–VII only. ⚠ **Fill fingerprint.** `gapProb` 0.60 / `descendProb` 0.40 / `rampJitter` 9 over 8th-triplets, even grouping, ramping 64–110 — the softest roll ceiling in the batch, which is what a record with very little fill activity should sound like when it does fill.
